claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 3339 s4.2: "Numeric offsets are calculated as \"local time minus UTC\". So the equivalent time in UTC can be determined by subtracting the offset from the local time." But its NOTE: "numeric offsets represent only time zones that differ from UTC by an integral number of minutes. However, many historical time zones differ from UTC by a non-integral number of minutes." So "Any zone's time" is too broad for the written offset. Zone-only half: prior .NET evidence.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc3339.txt s4.2 (lines 231-252); refs/dotnet-docs/docs/standard/datetime/time-zone-overview.md:25,31
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A local time can be expressed with its offset from UTC written after the time; +07:00 means the clock is 7 hours ahead of UTC, so subtract 7 hours for UTC. A local time with its offset identifies one instant; in a zone without daylight saving, the zone alone does.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 3339 s5.6 (profile of ISO 8601): "date-time = full-date \"T\" full-time", "full-time = partial-time time-offset", time-numoffset = ("+" / "-") time-hour ":" time-minute; "NOTE: ISO 8601 defines date and time separated by \"T\"." s4.4 "Unqualified Local Time": interpretation "will fail in approximately 23/24 of the globe". Prior .NET: "Unspecified date and time values have no time zone information."
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc3339.txt s5.6 (lines 399-437), s4.4 (lines 262-275); refs/dotnet-docs/docs/standard/base-types/standard-date-and-time-format-strings.md

issues.quote: Any zone's time can be expressed as an offset from UTC, written after the time
issues.text: Claim 3 (meta only) says any zone's time can be written as an offset; RFC 3339 s4.2 NOTE: numeric offsets represent only zones that differ from UTC by an integral number of minutes, and many historical zones do not. Lesson body (s3 'offset' bullet) does not say 'any', so no body change is needed.
issues.fix: Replace claim 3 text in .meta.json with the suggested_text in claim_verdicts n=3. No change to en.md or vi.md.

issues.quote: The lab is the set of Đơn Hàng programs that `scripts/up.sh` starts on your own machine, database included; in its database, the `orders` table has one row per order and one column per fact
issues.text: 'Database' is not in what I know. From this sentence and 'PostgreSQL, the lab's database' I can infer it is one of the lab's programs and keeps tables of rows, which is enough to follow, but the word itself is never given a meaning.
issues.fix: Add a short appositive at first use: 'database included, the program that keeps Đơn Hàng's data in tables'.

issues.quote: the date would come from the zone PostgreSQL applies to each connection, a setting whoever connects can change
issues.text: 'Connection' to PostgreSQL is not explained. From TCP I can guess it means one program or person talking to the database, but I cannot tell who 'whoever connects' is in the lab (me, via run-query.sh?).
issues.fix: Replace 'each connection, a setting whoever connects can change' with 'each program or person talking to it, a setting each of them can change'.

issues.quote: On .NET 10, with the sample run as shipped, `FindSystemTimeZoneById` finds Vietnam's zone by the same name the database uses
issues.text: 'with the sample run as shipped' hints that some other setup might not find the name, but I am not told what could differ, so I stop and wonder whether my own run could fail.
issues.fix: Drop 'with the sample run as shipped,' or add one clause saying the reader needs to change nothing for the name to be found.

issues.quote: local time — a date and a clock reading, such as 06:20 on 31 March; it names an instant only once you know its offset, or its zone if that zone never moves its clocks.
issues.text: This bullet uses 'offset', 'zone' and 'moves its clocks' before the bullets that define them, so on first read the second half made no sense to me. The Core concepts terms are also not bold, so I cannot find them at a glance later.
issues.fix: Move the local time bullet after the offset bullet, and bold each term at the start of its bullet.

issues.quote: So `placed_at` holds a moment, not a date.
issues.text: Core concepts defines 'instant', but the lesson switches between 'instant' and 'moment' (and quiz q1 uses both). I paused to check whether a moment is something different from an instant.
issues.fix: Use 'instant' consistently where the defined idea is meant, e.g. 'So `placed_at` holds an instant, not a date.'

issues.quote: Of the result's 11 rows, two pair different dates: `2026-03-12` with `2026-03-13`, and `2026-03-30` with `2026-03-31`.
issues.text: I had to re-read this paragraph: it goes from the two odd rows, to order 5, to the 12 March counts, then switches to what happens without AT TIME ZONE. The last point feels squeezed in.
issues.fix: Start a new paragraph at 'The query names the zone each time.'

issues.quote: The lab is the set of Đơn Hàng programs that `scripts/up.sh` starts on your own machine, database included; in its database, the `orders` table has one row per order and one column per fact, and that moment sits in `placed_at`.
issues.text: This one sentence defines the lab, the database, the table, rows, columns and placed_at at once; I read it twice before the story continued.
